utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber has received copies of some e-mail exchanges between the parties and understands that the Defence - but I'm seeking confirmation from all Defence teams - would not mind if you, Mr. Re, would further examine in chief the present witness also on -- well, let me say Sanije Balaj, but that Defence would not cross-examine the witness. The Chamber would add to that that it still might be an option - I'm very careful in not suggesting anything further than what the Defence expressed - that if you would include part of the cross-examination on the Sanije Balaj issue already, you would not, by doing so, lose the right to recall the witness for further cross-examination on Sanije Balaj. I leave it in the hands of the Defence. I leave it entirely in the hands of the Defence because postponement is, as such, justified. At the same time, if there's any chance that by doing some of the cross-examination today we could avoid that we unnecessarily have to recall the witness, that of course would be preferable. There's no need to further explain or to further -- what position you will take. But as I said before, I leave that in the hands of the Defence. It's is accepted if you do not it's also accepted in you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we revisit that issue a little later in the afternoon. I ought simply for Your Honours' information indicate that during the course of the later part of the morning today, the Prosecution disclosed to the Defence the full transcript of the proceedings in Kosovo which arrived I think at just five minutes before 1.00. I'm not at the moment clear as to the circumstances that lay behind that material being in the Prosecution's possession and not disclosed, but I don't pursue that at this stage. In addition to that Your Honour will recall that yesterday afternoon Mr. Re indicated that the Prosecution was in possession of the investigation file in respect of the death of Sanije Balaj which had culminated in the prosecution in Kosovo. I understand, and I can perhaps invite Mr. Re to confirm the position in respect of that, that efforts have been made today between the Prosecution and UNMIK to seek UNMIK's consent to the disclosure of that material to the Defence as well. So I maintain the position, although this is not the time to pursue it, I maintain the position that there is evidence of a systems failure in respect of the handling of disclosure of this material and at an appropriate moment I would want, if I may, to have an opportunity to address the Bench in relation to that. But I don't seek to do it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I also understood Mr. Re would highly appreciate before putting the matters before the Court that he's always willing to listen to you first, so which then makes it not necessary to use strong words in both directions in court. Mr. Re, I have not asked you yet, I think it fits more or less in your initial proposal that you would examine the witness in chief also on Sanije Balaj, and that if need be cross-examination could be separated in two parts. Are you still, because I don't know whether you're prepared to continue your examination-in-chief dealing with the Sanije Balaj issue as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can do that. The only slight complication is this, that I personally became aware that we had the UNMIK -- or we had the entire trial transcript basically about -- probably about 15 minutes before I sent it to the Defence, and I've reviewed it -- we've reviewed it. And it's really little different to the investigation statement, which the Defence have had for -- I think since February from the witness. So in that sense, I mean, I can lead the evidence. I understand the Defence wishes to conduct their own inquiries before cross-examining. We don't have -- we have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand now the Defence says we'll have a further look at it. We'll see how far we could go today. We'll consider that, and perhaps later this afternoon the Defence will inform us on whether the suggestion by the Chamber to go as far as possible this afternoon would be followed or whether postponement of the cross-examination entirely would be their preference. Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's just one very minor matter in relation to the 92 ter statement yesterday and an order made in to it relation. It may be of little consequence now that Mr. Re may be posing to lead evidence in relation to Sanije Balaj, but on page 5700 of the transcript at between lines 2 and 7 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just allow me one second to open that portion of the transcript. Could you please repeat the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Page 5700, at the very top between lines 2 to 7. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: It's a very minor matter, but it should be the last two sentences of that paragraph should be deleted, whereas Your Honour said just the final sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said it should be the two last sentences?

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: You ordered -- you ordered it was the last sentence of paragraph 85 to be taken out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Which reads: "Such things are not supposed to happen," in fact it should be the previous sentence as well which was also taken out at that time, so just for clarity on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do agree with you. I overlooked -- that is a very short last sentence, whereas the part to be stricken starts with: "In the case of. " Thank you very much for your correction. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can also confirm what Mr. Emmerson said about the UNMIK file, the investigation file. Mr. Dutertre and I spoke to all three Defence counsel during the lunch -- well at lunch. We have received oral permission from UNMIK this afternoon to disclose the entire file. I hope to have everything we can possibly disclose in relation to Sanije Balaj to Defence today. We are making our best endeavours to disclose everything we possibly can today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: One further matter. A matter in relation to the standing order in relation to exhibits. Mr. Emmerson just informed me there is one map he intends to show, I take no issue with that. We received an e-mail at six minutes to 2.00 this afternoon from the Defence of the Brahimaj team indicating some ERNs and photographs of documents. Unfortunately it doesn't say whether they're exhibits. It's very difficult for us at six minutes to 2.00 to work out what documents the Defence is intending to use in cross-examination. I think the order specifies at the time the oath is taken and I assume Mr. Guy-Smith won't be putting any exhibits to the witness, because we haven't received any notification of it yet. MR.TROOP: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: That -- perhaps I can provide some explanation with respect to the late disclosure of documents we were intending to use in cross-examination. That was simply caused by the fact that we didn't expect this witness to be called and start testimony yesterday, as you were aware. A different witness was scheduled to testify yesterday. That explains the slightly late notification. I do apologise to Mr. Re. If he needs any assistance with what those particular photographs or documents are, I am happy to explain it to him on the break if that's any assistance to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, because a question has been asked, it was not my intention to put any exhibits to this witness because of what I believed we were going to be doing. If there's a modification with regard to examination then there would be a number of exhibits that I would potentially be putting to the witness. And what I will do is I will put together a list at this time to the extent that one can be put together. But this is part of the reason why I think at this juncture I probably will be maintaining the position that I took yesterday with regard to the cross-examination on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for all that. We'll see how far we can go, and of course I think there will be mutual understanding between the parties that due to the, could I say, disturbance of the order of evidence to be heard, that if time-limits are not met completely that this should not have dramatic consequences, and we should try to adapt as good as we can to this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and just one final matter, and I hope it will have become clear to Your Honours from the exchange of e-mails this morning that there is a witness who is scheduled to testify next week in respect of whom very similar questions may arise concerning the relevance of that witness's testimony to the Sanije Balaj case. And I thought it right that that should be brought to Your Honours' attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are aware of it. Mr. Re, are you ready then to -- to continue your examination especially in respect of that part that you were earlier prohibited to touch upon?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Krasniqi to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You might have expected that you would be cross-examined by the Defence, but there is -- there are some additional questions to be put to you by Mr. Re. Before you answer these questions, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony; that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon again, Mr. Krasniqi. I'm going to ask you questions this afternoon specifically about Sanije Balaj and what you know about what happened to Sanije Balaj. Okay.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand that you testified in the trial of Idriz Gashi in Kosovo on the 10th of May, 2007, in relation to the disappearance of Sanije Balaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about a time in August 1998 and your meeting of Sanije Balaj. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the elementary school of the village of Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was in your KLA headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the army was there, located in the school. We had three facilities of the school in which we were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And whereabouts were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day I was in school, the school was called Re, it was a new building. In that building I was with Nazif Ramabaja, and we -- we were talking together about something. We were in the new school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then two soldiers came. They knocked on the door. After they knocked on the door, we told them to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were two of my cousins, Avni Krasniqi and Iber Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told both of us - Nazif was -- Nazif was the commander - they said that there was a person who had been detained by the military police, and that person was a suspect. They wanted somebody to come to interrogate that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Nazif's response?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazif said, Very good. He said, I do not have that profession. He said that Suf [Realtime transcript read in error"Isuf"] had been working in that branch in the police, so he told he me to go and interrogate that person. Suf not Isuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he tell you what this person was suspected of, why she was a suspect?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they said that they had stopped this person while going to Peje. Her goal, according to them, was that she wanted to buy a telephone with an antenna. However, she would go from Strellc to Peje through Rahovec and that was more difficult than going through Lugu i Baranit, Qallapek, and Trucuja [phoen]. So the reason she took this other route were the basis of their suspicions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did they suspect her of?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They found a notebook in her possession. She had some addresses on the notebook. They said that they knew her and they suspected her of working for a Serb, his name was Corovic Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the addresses in the notebook Serbian?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not in Serbian. They were in Albanian, but we know the name Corovic Dragan is a Serbian name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that they told you -- or they told Nazif they wanted someone to come and interrogate her. Where was she when they said this to you, that is, when they came to the office and told you they wanted someone to interrogate her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in the old school. We called it red school, it was an elementary school. In that school there was the police, the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go there with your two cousins to see her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Upon receiving the order I went, together with my two cousins, we went directly to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your two cousins in uniform?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not complete uniforms, half uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had -- they had light weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said this woman was in the old school in -- or you called it the red school. Whereabouts was she in that part of the old school?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go from Peje to Qallapek and Gllogjan, the school is the first building on the left. It is at the entry. It's almost at the end of the village of Baran. It's the first building on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whereabouts in the building was she when you went there with your two cousins?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there, it was the teachers' room. She was in the teachers' room. She was sitting on a chair.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was anyone with her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was another person. He was also sitting. I do not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a KLA soldier?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a soldier. He had a KLA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he also armed?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the woman free to leave the company of that KLA soldier in the school at that point?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there, but he did not talk to her. When I came inside I saw them both sitting. They stood up when I entered. We exchanged greetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Based on the information you had when you went there, was she free to leave at that point, when you went to interrogate her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she was not free. Of course she was not free. She was in the school, she was kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you recognise her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised her, only by face, not by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do when you went into the room and saw her there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we exchanged greetings, in a professional way, I asked her ID. I did not know her name. And then I took her personal details. After I noted down her personal information, I asked her what was the purpose of her trip, where she wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was her name?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her name was Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did she say to you when you asked her what the purpose of her trip was?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She told me that she wanted to go to Peje to buy a telephone. In Kliqine she said she had an aunt, she would go to her aunt, and then together they would go and buy a telephone. A telephone at that time cost about 250, 280 marks. She wanted to install a telephone in the village in order to make some profits.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else did you question her about?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the first part of the conversation. I asked her, Why don't you take a briefer route to Peje? Why did she -- had taken this longer route. It was about 33 kilometres longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was her response?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that she had set up the appointment with her aunt, and she said that her aunt was waiting for her and that this was a safer route.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response to that?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing to say to her. I told her that these boys suspected her, that she was a collaborator of that person. They had taken her. There was also another person with her, but that other person was released by the military police. She had been taken here. Then after I said those words, my two cousins intervened. They said that she was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were they in relation to you when you were questioning her? Just describe to the Trial Chamber where the four of you were in relation to this woman, Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting at a table like this. It was a bigger table. A teacher desk. It was in the middle of the room. I was sitting at the desk. She was sitting in front of me. Another soldier was on the left side, the one I found when I came in. She did not say any word. And my two cousins, they stood on the left side. They stood close to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said your two cousins intervened and said that she was not telling the truth. What was her response or your response to their intervention?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that this is the truth, this is my purpose. I told them it is not right for them to intervene and I told them to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told your two cousins to go out; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they go out?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went out. They obeyed and went out. But when they went out the floor, the floor was with planks, so I could hear that they were not far away, they probably were eavesdropping to what was being said in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you continue the interrogation of Sanije Balaj after your two cousins left?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I took her personal information, I told her that it is not right for her to go to Peje. I told her that there were some suspicions. So until these suspicions were actually thrown light on, she could not go to Peje. Then she again said that she was telling the truth. I told them that we cannot take a statement from her because there was no woman present. We simply took her personal data. So if we wanted to get more information from her, we should go to her village in order to talk to her there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you tell her she would require permission to go to Peje?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told her that if she wanted to go to Peje, she should go to the staff in the village in order to get permission for her to go through our area and to reach the other area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Staff, do you mean KLA staff?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There was a staff in her village, in the village of Strellc.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards we interrupted the whole thing. It lasted for about five minutes only. Since she was kept there, I told her that she could go at lunchtime. She said, No. And then I told her that we would provide food and also transportation to her so that we could take her safely to her village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you the person then in charge of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military police we had Hasan Gashi. I went there only to take the interview in Baran. In Baran I was the one, yes, in the school. .

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just clarify this. The school where you interviewed her, was that part of the military police or part of another part of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school was given to the military police. Some young men, our best selected young men, would stay there in order to do their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the military police based in the part of the school where you interviewed or interrogated Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there. Fortunately, on that day, Hasan was not there. He was, by profession, policeman like me. So in his absence they sent me as a professional in order to make the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, a moment ago you said you would provide her with food. Did you or your soldiers give her lunch?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she did not accept anything. So I could not give her food if she rejected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have transportation -- I withdraw that. I'll come to that in a moment. Approximately how long did your interrogation of Sanije Balaj last?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, the whole conversation took no more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see the notebook yourself which had the Serbian name in it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you assess the name -- or what was the significance to you, as an experienced investigating police officer, of seeing a Serbian name in her notebook?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was normal. There was nothing to have any suspicion. It was not only her who had such notebook. There were also other people with notebooks in which they had written down Serbian names.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who showed you the notebook? Was it her or someone else?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had the notebook. They told me, Look what kind of notebook she had. And then I said, Can I see it? And then she gave it to me. I wanted to see with my own eyes, and then I asked her also about the money. And then she showed me the money which really proved to me that she intended to go and buy the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of notebook was it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I was not very much interested. It was a small notebook. I was not interested to look at it carefully. I never thought it would be important for me to remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, do you know a person called Galani?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised this person later. I had seen him several times. His nickname was the one you mentioned. After 2000, 2002, I learned his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he there that day?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, he was on my left side. He was in the room I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He was the third person whose name you didn't give us before. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the third person who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his position in the KLA then? Was he a military police officer?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember his position. I know that he introduced himself as Officer Galani. I know nothing more about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to the transportation. You said you offered her transportation home. What transportation did you have available?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- we had a Lada, an old car. Then we had also a truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have any military police vehicles?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish I had, but that is not true. We had only private cars. We had no military vehicles. We had only private cars of different colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later she refused to come to lunch. I repeated once again my invitation. I told her that the vehicle had gone to take lunch to other places, and then I told her that when the vehicle would come back we would accompany her. She said no. And then I asked the other people there who were present if they had a vehicle. They told me that they had a red Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you referring to your two cousins, Avdi and Iber Krasniqi, are they the people you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did she go?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that she knew them. They will take me home, that's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did she go with those two in their red Golf?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went out of the room. She wanted to take her things. I told her that I have no time to stay. She went with them. I went halfway, then I saw the car. She was in the car and the car left in the village -- in the direction of the village of Baran, towards her village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, was that the last time you saw Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the last time I saw her. I saw her entering into the car, and then I saw her no longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it brought to your attention at some later point that she never made it back to her village?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear happened to her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an attack there, there were daily attacks. I was in the village of Gramaqel, Baballoq. I returned. When I returned, I heard that somebody from Strellc had been detained. After the offensive, after Gllogjan was occupied, I met with her brother. After about two weeks, some soldiers told me that somebody had come to meet me at the school. I told them to bring the person inside. He refused. He was unshaven. He had an automatic rifle in his hand, a Kalashnikov; I had nothing with me. I went up to him, and I told him that he should come inside. I exchanged greetings with him. After we exchanged greetings, I asked him to go inside the school in order to discuss why he had come there; he refused. Then I offered him to go into a bar that existed nearby; he refused. Then I said, I'm sorry. I don't know why you have come, but I cannot talk to you in the street. If you want to come and talk to me, let's go in an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, was that her brother, Shaban Balaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This was Shaban Balaj, his brother -- her brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did he say to you when you spoke to him in the office about his sister?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not go into the office at all. We stood somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he say to you about his sister?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I refused to talk to him in the street, I will tell you what I said to him and what we did. I told him, Because you have your vehicle here, we can get into the vehicle and we can discuss whatever you want in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have a discussion with him in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what he -- the subject of the discussion was in relation to his sister?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Prosecutor, I will tell you because it's very important. Although I had personal problems caused by this until the truth came out. There was a charge against me for something that I never did or never committed; however, I will tell you about the things we discussed, and I will speak about myself later. After we got into the car, I saw that the person was not aggressive. However, I could understand that he was looking for a person of his own family -- everybody would do that. He went into the car first, and the barrel of his gun was directed in the other side, not towards the side that I entered the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you please tell the Court what he said and what you said.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he had come to learn about his sister, where his sister was. He said, I know that she has been to Baran. I have talked to other people and I know that you have questioned her, so I need to know where she is now. First he did not mention her name, but later when I asked who this person was, he gave me the name. And I said to him, Very well. And I took out my notebook and I read the name, the surname, and the full details, and I asked him, Are you asking about this person. And he said, Yes. And I said, Okay. And I told you everything I told you earlier. That day I was with Nazif Ramabaja in the school. Two of my cousins came there, they were members of the military police. They thought that she was suspicious and asked me to interview her. I interviewed her, and she was released. That's what I told him. She was released to go to her own village, to her own house. And if we would have something to ask her about, we would go again to her village and ask her questions. He said, Thank you very much. And he said that he had heard some words, some rumours, and he also said that if she was a collaborator of the Serbs, he would kill her with his own hand, nobody else needed to kill her. We greeted each other, and he seemed satisfied with my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he tell you what the rumours were that he had heard?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't at that moment, but he had come to look for her thinking that she was there, and also that he had been looking for me but I had not been there. This was the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that the end of your discussion with Mr. Shaban Balaj about his sister?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that day, yes, that was the end of the discussion, and there is another thing. I told him to go and meet those two people who accompanied her and the third person as well, because they know where she went to. I did not know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do in relation to investigating what had happened to Sanije Balaj after she left the custody of the KLA in Baran when you saw her on that day in August 1998?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I did not know that something had happened to her. I just waited and wanted to hear whether I could get any information from her -- for her. But then there were attacks, so I couldn't do anything in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were any investigations conducted in relation to her disappearance?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: By who?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation was carried out in Prapaqan. Nazif Ramabaja came and he told me that I needed to go to Prapaqan to give a statement regarding Sanije Balaj, who is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did Nazif Ramabaja come to know about it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had been in Prapaqan that day. He came back from Prapaqan to me and he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you who conducted the investigation, and you said Nazif Ramabaja told you you needed to go to Prapaqan to give a statement. Who were you supposed to give the statement to, or who was conducting that investigation?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who was conducting the investigation was Fadil Nimoni.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil Nimoni was a soldier in the KLA. He was a very good man. He had the nickname Tigri, the tiger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in the military police?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, at that time he was assigned to the military police and was the person who was assigned to conduct the investigation. But then, unfortunately, he was killed in the war in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he a commander of the special military police?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I understood at the time, that he was a commander of the military police in Prapaqan --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me Mr. Re, I don't believe that there's been any evidence that there is a special military police. The military police, but nothing special about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Special" doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anything special about the military police?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing special, because to be special, Mr. Prosecutor, they had to do other jobs as well. This was a normal military police, something that we had at the time to carry out those duties. In order to have a proper military police, we would have needed years.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was Tahir Zemaj involved in this investigation in any way?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed, all of us together, about what happened, and in a way, all of us were interested to learn the truth about her fate and what happened to her. Tahir Zemaj did not question anyone or interrogate anyone about this. Tahir Zemaj himself died later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "we," "we discussed," you mean you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself, Nazif Ramabaja, we were together. And when he told me that I had to go and give an interview, I started to question myself, what did I do? Because rumours spread so quickly on the ground and I was thinking maybe people think that I killed her or I did something to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just -- let's go back to Tahir Zemaj. Did you -- when you said "we discussed," was Tahir Zemaj part of any of those discussions?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I was there, he was engaged in a conversation with some other people. I told them that I did not have much time to stay, so I entered first to give the interview and then I left Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Tahir Zemaj aware of this investigation and the fact that you were going to Prapaqan to be interviewed?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened at Prapaqan? Did you give a statement to someone or were you interviewed by someone or what happened?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I entered first the office where Fadil Nimoni, the late Fadil Nimoni, and he started by saying that, You have spoken to this person. You interviewed her. There were some people present there that I did not know, and I said, If we need to talk about this, these people do not need to be present here because this is an investigation. And he said, These are my friends, there is no problem. And because I was much more prepared than he was in such matters, I smiled and I said, Okay, whether -- because you are assigned to do this job, let's go on, let's do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I just want you, if you can possibly focus on who you spoke to and what you said, whether a statement was taken or an interview, just the formal process.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that according to his opinion I had not done my job. And I said, How can you know if you were not there? And he said, Well, if you had done your job properly, then you would have something written down. And I said, I did not write anything down except her details because we did not have a female there present that had to be present while interviewing her. And that's how I acted. He said, Well, you should have found someone. And I said, I couldn't, and that's why I told her to go to her own home and then we would talk to her in her own home. And I said that was all. He said, Well, you have not done a good job. My response was that I did not have time, and I did not have the means to conduct a better job, as you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did -- was a record taken of your conversation or questioning by Mr. Nimoni?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, notes were being taken, but I don't know. I think they were burnt. I think all the notes got burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did his questioning of you last?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long because I did not have much to say to him. I only told him that I let her go and there were these people who accompanied her. I told him that this is how I acted and that I released her. Whether this was good or bad, that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The two people, did you tell them -- you've said before it was Iber Krasniqi and Avni [Realtime transcript read in error"Avdi"] Krasniqi, your cousins. Did you see them there in Prapaqan on that day?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Avdi, but Avni. It's reflected wrong there in the transcript and that's another person. The second name Avdi, it should not be Avdi, but Avni.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's corrected. Were Avni and Iber Krasniqi in Prapaqan when you were there on that day?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of them were there. Avni's brother, Mete Krasniqi, was there as well. He's also dead now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Galani, was he there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what's Galani's name?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I learned that Galani's name was Idriz Gashi, who for a time -- who for a long time used to live in Sweden. He came back from Sweden, and these are things that I learned after the year of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is he the person on trial in Kosovo at the moment for the murder of Sanije Balaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the person that is being prosecuted. He was arrested last December. I insisted, because I was a suspect myself and I said, They ask me questions, why don't they ask questions to people that were last with her? They let them go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the people you have told the Court were last with her -- that you saw last with her are Iber and Avni Krasniqi. You say you saw them in Prapaqan on the day that you went to speak to Mr. Nimoni, and they were your cousins. Did they tell you whether or not they had also been questioned by Mr. Nimoni or anyone else about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not tell me anything. It was morning. We just greeted each other, and they just asked me, Have they called you as well? And I said, Yes. I went in first, I left, and I don't know what happened after.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You never spoke to them afterwards about what they said to Mr. Nimoni or anyone else there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't speak with them about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In all these years?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these years, I never spoke to them about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what did you hear happened to Sanije Balaj and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. That's a very general question in the context of the witness who has given evidence in an ongoing trial. He may have heard anything in any context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, could you please be more specific and ask whether and from whom the witness learned anything about what happened to Sanije Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to 1998. Did you hear anything in 1998, that is, after you last saw her, about what had happened to her; and if so, who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know from whom, but I heard people say that she had disappeared, somebody said that she had been killed, somebody said otherwise, but I did not pay too much attention. Because there were no concrete names said. So I did not pay too much attention to that. And if I got involved in the investigation, then people might think that I was involved in some way in her disappearance. So I just waited.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's just go back. You said that her brother, Shaban Balaj, came and spoke to you. How long after you last -- or the time you saw her when she got into the red Golf with your cousins was that?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. Two or three days, because as I said I lost my notes and for that reason, without my notes, I cannot give you an answer. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the brother -- from what you've said, the brother came to you and had some information that you had spoken to her and you had the notebook. Did he tell you how he got the information that he knew that you had spoken to her in the -- or interrogated her in the school?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers or other people had told him. I don't know who exactly. He had also asked in my village because a cousin of his, a female cousin, is married to one of my cousins. And he said that, I asked in your village about you. I've heard good words about you in your village, and he said that, If she fell in your hands, we are sure that you wouldn't do anything to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, we hear a lot of details of which the relevance and the importance is not entirely clear to the Chamber. Could you please focus on what's really the core of the matter, and I don't know how much time you would still need, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A few minutes. I'm almost there, several more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please try to do it as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether she was then living with her brother, that is, on the day she left the school after you interrogated her?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know where she lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did her brother give you any information about whether or not she arrived home after you sent her off with your two cousins to take her home?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He said that she had not arrived home and that he did not know where she was. And he also added that, If he suspected that she's a collaborator, I will kill her with my own hand. These are the things that I also have said in the court in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you signed yesterday, paragraph 85, you said: "In the case of her," Sanije Balaj, "there was an unfortunate execution without a fair trial. Such things are not supposed to happen." What did you mean by putting that in your statement which was -- which you signed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, after these things happened, we heard that one of these three persons who accompanied her had -- executed her without trying her and so on. So the responsibility lies with the people who were with her last and who have done it, not the people who have not done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just for clarity for the record and as my final question, the three people are Avni, Iber Krasniqi and Galani, that is Idriz Gashi?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These three were there, according to me. I don't know what happened. I did not see anybody do anything, but what I know for sure is that I left her in their care for the last time. So if anyone is responsible it's the people who were last with her and not me. I was the main suspect for this crime; although, I never committed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? If that's at least the order among Defence counsel you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is the order; and yes, I am ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I'm not going to ask you any questions at the moment about Sanije Balaj. I may come back to that later but I shan't be asking you a great deal about that today. I want to go to some of the more general evidence that you've given about the organisation of the KLA in the areas where you were a member and the relationship between those areas and the command structures that you've described. Now, and you were asked yesterday a number of questions about passages in your witness statement and the various maps that you have either produced or marked, I want to just see if I can get the picture clear and in the right chronological order. Now, and in your witness statement at paragraph 24, I'm just going to read to you the passage -- I don't know whether you have the witness statement with you in Albanian, do you? I think you're just about to be provided with it. Perhaps make sure we're using the same document, use the one the usher provides you with. I'll just let you find paragraph 24 for a moment. Now, the wording of the translation may not come through exactly the same as the written translation, but the record in paragraph 24 begins with a description of the death of your cousin, Adrian Krasniqi, and then continues in the following sentence as follows: "Because of the Serb repression, we started organising ourselves in small groups to face the Serb repression. Since I was a former police officer, I started training recruits in shooting, operations, and tactics. Just before the Serb attack on the village of Vranoc, on the 29th of May, 1998, we were just a group, but after this attack the village chose me as a commander." And I just want to see if I can understand in a little bit more detail then what the organisation was in the area where you were around Vranoc up to the 29th of May. So first of all, is it right that up to the 29th of May the villages were just small groups?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true, due to the daily repression. After the attack on Gllogjan, three young people were killed. Then in February the Serbian forces began their deployments. They started to shell with heavy artillery. Then we realised that they had not come for our goods. If you want to use a language of guns, that means you have a different goal from what one should have thought. So we were forced willingly or unwillingly. I have been an illegal in Kosovo for ten years since the attacks started. So I could tell you freely that if you are not able to go out in your place to have a job, then what can you expect? Better to die than to stay hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pausing there, Mr. Krasniqi. What I'm interesting in is the organisation and command structure, if there was one, in the area where you were before the 29th of May. Because you say in your statement that it was after that attack that you were chosen as a commander. May I ask you: Was there a commander in Vranoc before that attack?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interpretation please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll put the question again. Your statement says that it wasn't until after the 29th of May attack that you were elected or chosen by the village as the commander. And what I was asking you is whether there was a command structure in your village before that attack.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no -- there was nothing. We were only some young people, but nobody was designated who would be our commander. We were some young people in the village. I was the oldest one, Din, Mete, and some others. So we tried to get some weapons. We had 13 guns; with such weapons you cannot have a command. This was only to defend the village, so if the police would attack, then we would return the fire and give time to the population to flee the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that remained the position, really, up until the end of May, did it, in your area?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my area until 29th of May, this was the situation as I described. In Lumbardh, in Decan, in Katradiq [phoen]. In that direction we exercised our activity. For many years nobody had gone to the Yugoslav Army, so they had no information about weapons. So we wanted to prevent any unnecessary killings, so young people would learn how to use a weapon how -- so that they could not injure their friends. So on 29th of May we had this attack which started from the early hours of the morning. We were surrounded from all sides --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause there. I'm going to ask you a little later about the attack on Vranoc itself. At the moment I'm just focusing on the process of organisation in the area prior to that. And if we could just look a little further on to paragraphs 30 and 31 of your statement. You describe there the way in which you became involved in February and you say that: "In February Din Krasniqi and his cousin Mete Krasniqi" -- I'm sorry, "Din Krasniqi sent his cousin Mete Krasniqi to your house in Vranoc and you met Mete and that he told you that Din wanted you to join the KLA." From paragraph 31 you say from that day on, that is in February, you started training in Vranoc and that at that stage Din Krasniqi was UCK commander for Vranoc and later the Baran valley. I just want to understand that. If there was no formal command structure in Vranoc in February, what do you mean by the comment that Din Krasniqi was the commander for Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simple. When Mete came to me, Mete is no longer living, he explained me the situation. He said that he was sent by Din. He said that I was a person with experience with weapons, so we should get weapons in order to defend ourselves like other villages were doing. At that moment he told me that they had nobody to select, so we decided that Din would be the commander. That's what he told me. I said, Okay. He said that I should help him. He said that he is a doctor, you are a policeman, so probably this was a way in order to train young people. I said it's no problem. I started to do what I was asked. I said that we had no weapons, but he told me that we had two or three guns and that's how we started. We have no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where you say in paragraph 31 that there were 17 villages in the Baran valley, is it fair to say that in that area what was springing up were separate, spontaneous village defences like the one in Vranoc, with people like yourselves trying to organise with what weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the purpose. At that time there were 17 villages in Lugu i Baranit. More than half of them have no weapons; however, each of the village organised itself independently. They set up their own defence, based on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we then drop down to paragraph 33 which you were asked about yesterday, and I think Judge Orie asked you some questions about it in particular, in terms of the relationships between the villages and in that instance Jablanica. Paragraph 33 says: "The office of Din Krasniqi was located at his house in Vranoc village. He also had a private clinic at this place." And then you say: "In February 1998, not many people had uniforms. Most of them were training in civilian clothes. In February 1998, it was a known fact that an army existed in Jablanica under the command of Lahi Brahimaj. Din Krasniqi had visited Jablanica, and being a trust-worthy person, he was allowed to call himself as the commander of the Baran valley." And then you say this: "In February, there was no Dukagjini Zone in place, and at that time there was no commander of the whole area later called the Dukagjini Zone." Now, I want to suggest to you that that remained the formal position, i.e., that there was no formal, full Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone and no overall commander for the Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone until Ramush Haradinaj was elected as zone commander on the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. It is true. There was no commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I then ask you, please, against the background of the description that you have given us of the villages and the way in which they were spontaneously organising, just to help us how we should read paragraph 44 of your statement. Could you perhaps turn to paragraph 44 and just read it to yourself. I won't take time reading the whole paragraph into the record, but you refer there to different ranks within each village. Perhaps you just remind yourself of what is written there and help us to understand how that description fits with the description you've given us of spontaneous village defences springing up.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know which of the statements. I began giving statements starting from 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just the statement you have got in front of you at this moment, Mr. Krasniqi, you are asked to comment about and it is paragraph 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, you're quite right to observe that you've given a number of statements and this document has been cut and pasted together from different statements that you've made. But on the face of it, you seem to be describing an organisational command by reference to March 1998 in which each village has a general commander, a deputy commander, an operations commander, a logistics commander, a commander of the guards, and so forth, with different functions and tasks. Now, that does not, on the face of it, seem to reflect very closely the description that you've given us in February, March, and up to May of villages trying to get together and organise village defences as best they could. Sounds rather more formal than that. Can you perhaps explain that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every village after we could get some weapons, the village then decided to appoint in a village. This did not happen at all the villages at the same time. It was done first in one village, and then this was followed by other villages. For example, my village or Buqan, they were earlier than us to get the weapons. So after they got the weapons, they decided a commander of the staff. The other village then waited because they had no weapons, so they were not able to organise the defence. If a village had one or two weapons, then they also set up the same thing. So this is how it happened, first one village and then the example was followed by the other village. This did not happen at the same time in all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Simply this before we break, Mr. Krasniqi. Just help us, if you can, to understand the reality. Are these titles that really meant anything or were they merely allocated titles for people to create the impression of an organisation that wasn't really there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, there were no ranks. We had no uniforms. However, we designated some people in order to be the people who could keep calm so that there was no conflict in the village. The conditions were such that we had no arm depot, no regular army, no people to have a regular army. Everybody was taking part voluntarily. Weapons were borrowed from other villages, and then the villages then sometimes collected the money in order to buy their own weapon. There were no ranks; they were simply appointments. In 1999 there was -- there were no such things, even then, let alone 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. Would it be a suitable time to have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It certainly would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber apologises for returning late. I hope that the parties are convinced that these late returns, where the Chamber urges the parties to be there on time, are often caused by meetings during breaks. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I want to just move on now to the process by which these various village defences sought to organise together over the months towards the end of May and beyond. First of all, we've heard some evidence in this court from Rrustem Tetaj. He's a man I think you knew reasonably well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you, by any chance, see his testimony at all? Did you follow it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't followed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, he's given evidence about a meeting that took place in Gllogjan at the end of May when the leaders from a large number of villages in the area all came together to try for the first time to coordinate their efforts and to set up four smaller subzones in the areas to the east of the main Peje to Gjakove road. Now, were you aware of a meeting - this would be just about three days before the attack on Vranoc that you've described by the Serbs - were you aware that there was a meeting that had taken place as a sort of first attempt at organisation?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time I was not there. I was providing training. I learnt about it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So at the time you didn't know about it, but you subsequently heard about it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I learnt later that some went there to discuss; however, I don't know what they discussed and what decisions they took.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we could just bring up on the screen Exhibit P266 very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst that's being brought up, Mr. Krasniqi, I'll just explain to you what it is you're going to see. This is a map on which Rrustem Tetaj, in his evidence, marked the areas covered by the four subzones that were agreed at the meeting on the 26th of May. It's just about to load, I believe. It may take us a little while, because maps take longer than documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if we can just zoom-in, please. And -- I think you've got it upside down, yes. It first loads upside down in the exhibit I'm afraid. Very well. And if you move down the map, a little bit further, please, until the -- yes, that's satisfactory. And then if we could just move to the left. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, those are the areas that were marked by Rrustem Tetaj as the first group of zones that were established at the 26th of May meeting, and can you help us, please, in relation to that. Did you understand at that time whether the area that you were in Vranoc was within a particular subzone? We can see that Mr. Tetaj has marked, it is falling just to the right-hand or eastern border of zone 3.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not heard. I was not there. I did not know that we belonged to that zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have any particular connection to Rrustem Tetaj at the end of May? Was there any particular command relationship with Rrustem Tetaj, as you understood the position?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only knew that he was in Gllogjan, but I did not know the position he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely understand that there may have been confusion, crossed-wires, on the ground. It's just a question of at this stage whether you were aware of him having any particular responsibility for an area that covered Vranoc, and your answer to that is you were not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that he came. When he came I was not there. He talked to Din Krasniqi in the village of Vranoc --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- but I was not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know a man called Gani Gjukaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard this name, probably I have seen him, but I did not know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And you didn't have any awareness that he had a particular responsibility for the area that's marked with a number 4?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not know that such zones were created. I had no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the next date I want to ask you about, leaving this map to one side now for a moment, the next date I want to ask you about is the 23rd of June, which I asked you about a moment ago. We've seen some minutes of a meeting on the 23rd of June in which Ramush Haradinaj was elected as the commander of the Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone. Again, from your recollection at the time, were you aware that such a meeting had taken place?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that some people went there. They discussed and I was told that they agreed to elect Ramush Haradinaj as commander, like in the film Spartacus.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That may be a reference that not everybody is familiar with; although, I know what you're referring to. In practical terms one of the things that I'm trying to explore with you for the Trial Chamber, and I'm going to ask you some specific questions about it as we move through this period is that in practical terms what that meant in terms of the chain of communication and operation on the ground. Now, you were asked a number of questions yesterday about a map that you had drawn showing various centres, three brigades and two staff HQs. I'll come to the map in just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be loaded whilst I get to it, it should be P352.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've also seen, Mr. Krasniqi, some orders establishing the three brigades, Prapaqan Brigade, the brigade at Baran, and so forth and your particular brigade under Nazif Ramabaja, orders that are dated between the 10th and the 12th of July. Just to help us get the chronology right, was it around about the 10th or 12th of July that those three brigades were established?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, when I made the sketch I was asked about the headquarters in Gllogjan and Jabllanice. These were local headquarters. After the officers came, we thought that now we have some officers. So we thought about setting up something in order to increase the morale of the people. So we designated three points, three locations, three schools, and in those three centres which were referred to as brigades, we deployed officers who had graduated from military academies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pausing there, I'm trying at this stage to concentrate on the dates. Now, the officers that you're referring to, you say "after the officers came," you are referring, are you, to the officers who had previously been senior officers in the Yugoslav Army who entered Kosovo along with Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the period of June and July, the sixth and seventh month. I don't remember exactly, but approximately that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just trying to help you remember, if you can, because it's relevant to some of the passages in your witness statement, to get the dates as clear as we can. Now, we've heard evidence - and I don't think there's any dispute about this - that Tahir Zemaj entered Kosovo with those officers sometime around the 23rd, 24th, or 25th of June, not before then. And we've seen, as I say, records establishing your brigade and the other two brigades on the 12th of July or between the 10th and the 12th of July. Now, again, it's important for interpreting your map and some of the other markings that you've given us. Are you here describing events and relationships as they existed after the establishment of those brigades on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I have nothing to add. It was July. We had designated the locations, bigger facilities, and the officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And it was on the 20th of July that the swearing-in ceremony took place you told us?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the village of Baran. I was there, too. We organised the ceremony on 12th -- 20th. I invited the officers to come from all areas. Some could not come because of fighting, so I told them, whoever was free was welcome to come. We made some video-recording, they exist, so that we could have some evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've seen some of that video-recording in the courtroom here, Mr. Krasniqi. And that was the process, would you agree, by which the officers who'd come with Mr. Zemaj, sometimes called FARK officers, became integrated within the KLA?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they came they had only UCK emblems. After September offensive, because they had stayed in different countries -- outside people could say that they were the FARK or UCK, but in Kosovo they all belonged to UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again so that we're clear, during this month of July there had been a major Serb offensive, a major battle, at Loxha in the first -- the end of the first week of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the last week of July, earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, no, I'm sorry. That may have been a translation issue. The end of the first week of July was what I was putting to you.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, end of the first week.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you are right, about 5th or 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there was another major Serb offensive through the area within a week or so of the swearing-in ceremony, was there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's just important to get our chronology clear. Now, looking at this map you've told us that it's depicting in a graphic way locations after the 10th or 12th of July, and we can see that you've described Jablanica as a staff HQ; and you've described Gllogjan as a staff HQ. And I just wanted to understand from your perspective as an officer on the ground in Baran, is that how you saw them as being on an equal footing and independent of one another, those two staff HQs?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that moment this was how it was, they were independent. The same was true of us. We had no means and each of us operated independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come back to that in a moment. Could you look at paragraph 40 of your statement where you described the aftermath of the Serb attack on the 24th of March, and in the last sentence of that statement -- sorry, that paragraph, paragraph 40, you say that: "After this incident, the village of Gllogjan became the most important UCK HQ after Jablanica." And I just wanted to understand, as an official or an officer on the ground, is that how you understood it at that point, that these were two independent HQs but with Gllogjan achieving an importance secondary to Jablanica? Is that how it appeared to you?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, when the attack on Gllogjan began, Jabllanice was quiet at that time, there was no attack. When the village of Gllogjan came under attack, there was a limited number of people who had some armaments. It was Ramush, his brothers, and his cousins. They at that time put up resistance. The Serbian forces entered the village, entered the school, they kidnapped some and kept hostage some children and some people --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry to interrupt you. I don't -- I wasn't asking you to give us a description of the 24th of March incident as you understood it, but of the relative importance of Jablanica and Gllogjan in the aftermath period. You said that they were independent of one another. I wanted to know how you saw them in terms of relative importance.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, myself, as everybody else, looked at it as a heroic village that put up a resistance, and after the storm and after the success, people have respect for the person who led that resistance. So Gllogjan, in the municipality of Decan, is the first village to be known to have put up a resistance in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did that make Ramush a sort of spiritual figurehead for people?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning people did not know, but they started to ask each other who was that person. And then he was a kind of a spiritual leader. In the beginning people, in fact, were expecting to see somebody, heavy-built person, somebody big in stature, but he was a normal person, and we could not bring somebody who had a big body, to present him as Ramush just because of what people had imagined him to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in practical terms, you tell us, and you've just said it a moment ago, these centres, these five centres that you've described were operating in a fairly independent manner from one another. Is that right.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Completely independently. Everything was spontaneous. People admired him because he achieved the success. And they trusted him fully. This is how the truth was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you were answering questions about this relationship between these different power centres in the period after the 11th of July yesterday, you said they were not linked. You said: "In Gllogjan there was Ramush. In Prapaqan it was Tahir. Each operated independently, which means that we did not have the means and the possibilities to communicate with each other." Then you said: "However, if there was a problem or if we wanted to send some information, we send a courier in order to ask for some help." And then you said this: "When I was in Baran, if I had some problems, then I send some soldier with a vehicle in order to ask for some help. I sent him to Ramush, to Lahi, or to Tahir, the one which was closer." And I wanted to understand that answer a little more. Are you telling the Trial Chamber that from where you were in Vranoc, any one of those three commanders would be regarded from your point of view as operating autonomously so that you could call them or contact them directly?
