utterances.text: Lahi Brahimaj at that time had no authority to appoint Dr. Krasniqi as any type of commander, did he?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't at that time, but every village appointed whoever the village liked. And the other village -- another village couldn't have any influence on that decision. So this depended on the village, not on Lahi or Ramush or anyone else's wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: It was important, was it not, for weapons to be handed over to someone who was considered trust-worthy and who was known to the person supplying the weapons, was it not?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because if you give it to someone who you don't trust, he might create a problem. That's why you give the weapon, you entrust this to someone you know, and this is how it was. You give the weapon to a reliable person who won't misuse it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: And Dr. Din Krasniqi was known to Lahi Brahimaj, was he not, because he was a well-respected doctor who had, in fact, treated members of the Brahimaj family?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only Lahi's family members, but he was respected by all the members of the area. He went to everyone who needed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop, let's -- if you are running out of time start to make the whole list of patients of Krasniqi -- of Dr. Din Krasniqi. Do you not understand what is happening at this moment? We have gone over this several times, well-respected doctor, do we have to know whether he has treated the measles of the children before we accept it? That is really not the way in which you should use your spare time. Please proceed for another minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: The results of the meeting was that the agreement that was reached was simply that Dr. Krasniqi was someone who could be trusted to be provided weapons by Lahi Brahimaj. Was that the agreement reached?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was trusted by him and he knew that he would give the weapons to people he trusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: You've suggested that Lahi Brahimaj was commander in Jablanica during 1998. I'm going to suggest to you that that is not correct. Lahi Brahimaj's position was simply as provider of weapons as part of his responsibility with the General Staff. Can you agree or disagree with that question?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I agree or not, this is how he was perceived. I told you, I didn't know what role he had and what position he had, but when people saw him they thought of him as you put it. They didn't know what role he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: There were other commanders in Jablanica at that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop, Mr. Troop, your time is over. You are again asking now questions to the witness where he said he didn't know about the existence of a General Staff. He has explained that Mr. Brahimaj was good in providing weapons. He didn't know anything about the task, and you now you say I put it to you as a part -- he has answered those questions and he now correctly tells you that he earlier testified that he didn't know about a General Staff and about the tasks and repeats what he said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. Perhaps I could just explain why I was asking that question because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, because it's seven minutes past 7.00. So I'm not asking for further explanation. I'm giving an opportunity to Mr. Re for a very limited couple of minutes and with the indulgence of interpreters, transcriber, and technicians to put some questions. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I also -- because of this, I may have been a bit harsh to Mr. Troop, he's the victim of that, he's the last one, I'm aware of that. At the same time what I say, and I'll say two words about it later on that addresses all parties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I want to you to answer these questions with as few words as possible. Firstly Mr. Emmerson asked you about an offensive in August when the Serbs came into Gllogjan. Did the KLA then re-take the area before another Serb offensive?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there -- were there two Serb offensives: One followed by the Serbs leaving and then the Serbs coming back in?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The Serbs entered once, destroyed it, set fire to it, and left the village. When they wanted they came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Secondly, the video-clip. Mr. Emmerson asked you about the video-clip with Sanije Balaj. Where were you - one-word answer, please - where were you when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the school, and we had a television there and the video-recorder and I saw it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long was the clip, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there commentary on it, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No comment about anything. I just saw a group of girls, as I already said, and I didn't know that she was there at the time. I was told later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see that video once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once, in the beginning. But then later I saw it another time --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No -- okay. Finally on that -- on the video, just confine yourself to the question. When was it in relation to when you interviewed Sanije, before or after and what period?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it before and I didn't know that she was in that recording. The second time was after it was shown on television and it was a very short. The whole group was there. This is all I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Guy-Smith asked you about a photo-board. In your statement to UNMIK, it appears they showed you a photo-board. Is that what you're referring to, UNMIK showing you the photo-board, rather than the Office of the Prosecutor showing you the photo-board?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were investigators. I gave you their names, and in the end when the trial in Peje was on, I was asked again to look at photographs and to -- to sign the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the photo-board for the Peje trial investigation, not for the ICTY one?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask them who they represented. I was asked, Who do you know from these people in the photographs? There were no names under the photographs. There were only numbers. I only marked the ones I knew and signed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith asked you about audiotaping. Is it the case the only audiotaping of an OTP interview was with the videolink on the 15th of May, 2007? Is that the only time that was audioed [sic]?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in Pristina, in the Prosecutor's office. I don't know what they had there. I was told that everything would be there, they would record everything. I just gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only interested in -- is that the only time it was audioed, when you spoke to the Prosecutors and like me and people in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the only time. There was once before with Shahzada Sultan. He had a cassette recorder and also a small piece of equipment, I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The last thing I want to ask you is Mr. Emmerson asked you about rumours about Sanije Balaj, and you responded, this is at page 63, that you thought that you were the one -- the rumours were that you were the one who had ordered her killed. My question to you: Is that -- was that because the -- was that because that she was suspected of being a Serb collaborator that people thought that you had ordered her killed?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people think in different ways, and of most concern to me was the fact that I was one of the suspects and that an indictment was raised against me. I have the indictment here, and here it says that I am the only suspect in that case. However, I never meddled with the investigation. I stayed a part of the investigation. And the rumours don't bear any weight with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, rumours are already a rather difficult matter to tackle in examination, but if you start asking what inspired the rumours, then it even becomes more difficult. Was this your last question? Yes. Has this triggered any necessity for further questions? Then since the Bench has no questions either, Mr. Krasniqi, this concludes your testimony. There is a possibility that at a later stage that the parties would like to ask you some additional questions. If that happens, you'll be approached again. I think under the present circumstances what I'd like to ask you is not to speak about your testimony and I'm seeking also the assistance of the parties, a general instruction for perhaps what could be a month is perhaps too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is a sensitive situation. Having begun to look at the evidence at trial, there are a number of different people involved in this investigation, all of whom at one time or another seem to have been blaming each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think, if I may say so, it would be wise for the witness to be given a pretty firm direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, you would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krasniqi, I instruct you, since there is a chance that you might be recalled, I cannot tell you how small or how large that chance is, that you should not speak about your testimony with anyone until the moment that you hear that you don't have to come back. Now, this specifically also applies to everyone, everyone as a witness, as an accused, as an investigator, whomever in relation to the ongoing procedures in Pec, even after these proceedings have been concluded. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Agreed. No problem. I will stand by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague and I wish you a safe trip home again. We adjourn and we'll resume Monday, the 18th of June, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II, I think. I can't read it, as a matter of fact, Mr. Registrar. Courtroom II, yes. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.19 p.m.,
